# Accreditation and directory-change checks

Every check the directory workbench runs before a change can reach the root's ceremony (PLAN-M52 R0–R7), in the
order each command runs them. A refusal names its check by the id in the first column, so a filer can reproduce
it from the published inputs. Nothing here signs anything: the workbench reads, proposes and checks, and only
five FROST shares and the SLH-DSA root, offline, make a proposal the directory. Rows marked *not built* are
named so that their absence is visible, not implied.

## Change requests — `ainra directory check-request`

| Check | Built | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `request-shape` | yes | The request is version 1 of `ainra/directory-change-request`, names one of the six types, carries no field outside the format at any level, and canonicalizes (its digest is the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON without `proofs`). |
| `root-key-roll` | yes | ROOT_KEY_ROLL is refused: it runs on its own track (PLAN-M52 step 9), which is not built. |
| `request-subject` | yes | `registrar` is a registrar id (ASCII lowercase letters, digits and `-`, at most 63) and `filer` is not empty. |
| `request-base` | yes | The current directory the request is checked against verifies under both roots (FROST Ed25519 and SLH-DSA). With no directory, the request is checked for the first epoch. |
| `moves-trust` | yes | A request that moves trust is refused: REGISTRAR_KEY_ROLL, or an ACCREDIT that changes a key or the status URI of a registrar already in the directory. It needs a declared offline approver set (D-088 R0; an ADR and a schema change, not built). |
| `subject-in-directory` | yes | WITHDRAW, DISTRUST_FROM_LEAF and REVOKE_DELEGATE name a registrar in the current directory; ACCREDIT names one that is not. |
| `delegate-owned` | yes | REVOKE_DELEGATE is filed by the registrar itself and carries the delegate certificate; the certificate is signed by that registrar's log root (SLH-DSA) as the current directory lists it, and its fingerprint is not already revoked. The fingerprint is derived from the certificate, never taken from the request. |
| `cutoff-monotone` | yes | DISTRUST_FROM_LEAF never lifts a cutoff or moves one later; an existing cutoff can only move earlier (until the owner rules otherwise, PLAN-M52 item 12). |
| `self-signature` | yes | A request a registrar files about its own entry (REVOKE_DELEGATE, its own DISTRUST_FROM_LEAF or WITHDRAW) carries a hybrid signature (Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65) over the request message by the registrar's CURRENT issuer key, as the current directory lists it. |
| `adverse-notice-chain` | yes | An adverse request (DISTRUST_FROM_LEAF or WITHDRAW filed against another registrar) carries a compliance record: at least two notices, numbered 1, 2, … in time order and at least 14 days apart, each named by its SHA-256, and a cure window that ends at least 30 days after notice 1 and before the request was filed (D-094 item 11). |
| `adverse-vantage` | yes | The compliance record reproduces the failure after the cure window ended, no later than the filing, from at least two vantage points on distinct networks, each report named by its SHA-256. |
| `adverse-grace` | yes | An adverse WITHDRAW comes only after distrust: the registrar already carries a distrust cutoff in epoch N, the record names a public breach record (notice 3 or later), and the request is filed at least 90 days after it, so holders have had time to move (D-094 item 11). |
| `entry-shape` | yes | An ACCREDIT entry is for the request's registrar, decodes every key at its exact size (Ed25519 32 B, ML-DSA-65 1952 B, SLH-DSA 32 B), carries status keys and a status URI, and sets no distrust cutoff. |
| `proof-of-possession` | yes | An ACCREDIT proves possession of every new key: a hybrid signature by the issuer key, a hybrid signature by the status key, and an SLH-DSA signature by the log root, each over the request message. |
| `accreditation-match` | yes | When a copy of the registrar's served `/accreditation` is given (`--accreditation`), the entry's keys and status URI equal it. |
| `prerequisites` | yes | An ACCREDIT of a new registrar carries the Standard §3 prerequisites as named file digests: the signed identical agreement, the independence attestation, the funded competitor monitor, and the audit with its date (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `test-root-only` | yes | Until a legal entity exists, an ACCREDIT is accepted only with `test_root: true`. |
| `live-endpoints` | *not built* | Not built here: the registrar's endpoints answer, `/witness-feed` serves a consistency proof, `status_uri` serves a list that verifies under the entry's status key, and the compliance probe reports COMPLIANT. These need the network and the workbench is offline; the probe (`make probe-drill`) measures them against a live registrar. |

## Proposals — `ainra directory propose` and `ainra directory check-proposal`

| Check | Built | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proposal-shape` | yes | The proposal is version 1 of `ainra/directory-proposal` and carries no field outside the format. |
| `proposal-base` | yes | Epoch N verifies under both roots, and the proposal names it: its base epoch and the SHA-256 of its signing bytes. A first epoch names no base. |
| `proposal-epoch` | yes | The proposal is for epoch N+1 exactly; no epoch is skipped. |
| `proposal-issued-at` | yes | The new directory's `issued_at` is later than epoch N's. |
| `proposal-schema` | yes | The new directory carries no field outside the frozen directory schema, carries no signature yet, and lists its entries sorted and unique. |
| `proposal-requests` | yes | Each request the proposal applies is listed under the SHA-256 it really has, passes every request check against epoch N, appears once, and is the only request about its registrar (several REVOKE_DELEGATE excepted). |
| `proposal-no-drop` | yes | Every entry of epoch N is still present unless a WITHDRAW in the proposal names it. |
| `proposal-cutoff` | yes | No distrust cutoff of epoch N is lifted or moved later. |
| `proposal-revocations-kept` | yes | Every delegate revoked in epoch N is still revoked. |
| `proposal-rederive` | yes | The new directory is exactly what epoch N and the listed requests produce, re-derived from those alone. |
| `proposal-diff` | yes | The human-readable diff, with the request each line cites, is exactly the re-derived one. |
| `proposal-digest` | yes | `signing_bytes_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the re-derived directory's signing bytes: the exact message the custodians sign. |

## Signing — `ainra directory assemble`

| Check | Built | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assemble-both-roots` | yes | Both root signatures — the FROST 5-of-9 Ed25519 aggregate and the SLH-DSA signature — verify over the proposal's signing bytes under the pinned roots; one alone is refused. |

## Publication — `ainra directory publish`

| Check | Built | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `publish-both-roots` | yes | The directory verifies under both pinned roots; a directory with one root's signature is refused. |
| `publish-next-epoch` | yes | Its epoch is exactly the archive's last epoch + 1, and the proposal was drafted on that last archived epoch (same digest). |
| `publish-approved` | yes | The directory is the approved proposal: same epoch, and the SHA-256 of its signing bytes equals the proposal's. |
| `publish-transcript` | yes | The ceremony transcript names that proposal (its digest), that directory (its signing-bytes SHA-256 and epoch) and both of its signatures, lists at least five distinct signers, and — when its published SHA-256 is given — hashes to it. |
